body.codeblock: TASK identifier '()' IS statement_block END TASK
body.p: JALv3 introduces the concept of TASKs, which are a form of co-operative multi-tasking. Unlike preemptive multi-tasking, where control passes from one task to another automatically, control passes only when a task explicitly yields. Tasks take no parameters.
The number of task slots is set with the TASK pragma, or with the compiler option -task:

The count includes the main program itself. To run the main program plus three worker tasks, use PRAGMA TASK 4. It is generally better to set this in the program than with the compiler option, because the number is unlikely to change.
A task is started with the _task_start statement. It may be started from the main program or from another task:

A task yields the processor with _task_yield. The scheduler is a deterministic round robin: each yield hands control to the next live task, and a task that returns, or falls off the end of its body, removes itself from the schedule:
The older SUSPEND keyword still works but is deprecated and produces a warning; use _task_yield instead.
Running tasks can be manipulated from the main program or from a task with these statements. Each names a TASK and accepts an optional empty parameter list:
Only one copy of a task body may run at a time. Do not start a task that is already live.

Task local variables are allowed only on the 32-bit targets, where every automatic local receives a unique static address. On the PIC back ends all procedures share one software frame area, so a suspended task's locals could collide with another task's; declaring a variable inside a TASK on those targets is an error. Keep task state in globals there. On every target, a task body runs on its starter's stack, so keep the frames shallow.
body.codeblock:
PRAGMA TASK 3
VAR BYTE a_count = 0 VAR BYTE b_count = 0
TASK task_a() IS a_count = a_count + 1 _task_yield a_count = a_count + 1 END TASK
TASK task_b() IS b_count = b_count + 1 _task_yield b_count = b_count + 1 END TASK
_task_start task_a() _task_start task_b() _task_yield _task_kill task_b()
